name: Web Dork Fuzzer (WDF)
summary: A Go-based command-line security research tool focused on web discovery and automated testing workflows.
details: WDF is a command-line tool written in Go for web discovery and automated testing workflows.
The project evolved from an earlier repository named web-dork-fuzzer, which is kept for history. WDF is the current version.

name: Secure Chat
summary: An experimental secure messaging application combining a Flutter frontend, a Rust cryptographic core, and a lightweight Go backend.
details: Secure Chat explores how an end-to-end encrypted messaging application can be structured across three languages: a Flutter client, a cryptographic core written in Rust, and a lightweight Go backend.
This is an experimental project under active development. It has not had a security audit and is not production-ready.

name: Writing an OS in Rust
summary: An educational project exploring low-level systems programming and operating system development using Rust.
details: A learning project that works through the fundamentals of operating system development in Rust, running on QEMU.
It is an ongoing learning project, not a complete or production operating system.

name: Pwn College Writeups
summary: A collection of technical writeups documenting practical cybersecurity challenges completed through pwn.college.
details: Each writeup records how a pwn.college challenge was approached: reading the challenge, analysing the program, debugging, and the lessons learned along the way.
The writeups aim to be reproducible explanations rather than flag dumps. They are also published on this site under Blog.

name: Byte Scout
summary: A personal learning-oriented command-line project intended to support binary analysis and reverse engineering workflows.
details: Byte Scout is a Python command-line project built while learning binary analysis, intended to support reverse engineering workflows.
It is experimental and still in development.

name: SentinelAI
summary: An experimental project exploring the feasibility of using lightweight AI agents to assist with cybersecurity monitoring and defensive security workflows.
details: SentinelAI explores whether lightweight AI agents can assist people with cybersecurity monitoring and defensive security workflows.
It is an early-stage experiment. It is not a fully autonomous system and has not been deployed.
